'''Pushpa Mittra Bhargava''' (22 February 1928 – 1 August 2017) was an Indian scientist, writer, and administrator. He founded the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]], a federally funded research institute, in [[Hyderabad]]. He was outspoken and highly influential in the development of [[scientific temper]] in India, and argued that scientific rationalism needed to be cultivated as a civic duty.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thehindujobs.com/thehindu/jobs/0104/05180014.htm |title=The Hindu Opportunities : An interview with Dr. Pushpa Mittra Bhargava, recipient of the Padma Bhushan |access-date=2012-11-07 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121208020036/http://www.thehindujobs.com/thehindu/jobs/0104/05180014.htm |archive-date=2012-12-08 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ccmb.res.in/about_profile.html |title=About CCMB > Profile |publisher=Ccmb.res.in |date=1977-04-01 |access-date=2012-08-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120831194558/http://www.ccmb.res.in/about_profile.html |archive-date=2012-08-31 }}</ref>

==Life==
===Early life===
Bhargava was born in [[Ajaymeru]] ([[Rajasthan]]) on 22 February 1928 in a middle-class family, to Ram Chandra Bhargava, a medical doctor and public health professional, and his wife, Gayatri Bhargava. At age ten, his family shifted to [[Varanasi]],<ref>{{Cite web|title = Architect of Modern Biology – BioSpectrumIndia|url = http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/158338/architect-modern-biology|website = www.biospectrumindia.com|access-date = 2015-10-29|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140227065119/http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/158338/architect-modern-biology|archive-date = 27 February 2014|url-status = dead}}</ref>  where he was formally admitted to Besant Theosophical School directly to class nine. Until then he was [[home educated]] under the tutelage of his grandfather. After school, he completed intermediate from Queen's College, one of the best institutions in Uttar Pradesh at that time.<ref name="pmbmemoirs">{{cite web|title=PMB Memoirs: Nine decades of PM Bhargava|url=http://pmbhargava.com|website=PMB Memoirs|access-date=29 July 2016}}</ref> He received his B.Sc. in 1944 with Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and obtained an M.Sc. degree in 1946 in organic chemistry. He joined [[Lucknow University]] for doctoral programme and earned Ph.D. in synthetic organic chemistry in 1949, at age 21.<ref name ="pmbmemoirs"/>

===Career===
After completing Ph.D. at Lucknow University, Bhargava moved to Hyderabad.<ref name ="kalyane">{{cite journal|last1=Kalyane|first1=V.L.|title=Scientometric Portrait of P. M. Bhargava|journal=Lucknow Librarian|volume=27|issue=1–4|pages=42–70|url=http://eprints.rclis.org/4831/1/K-42.pdf|access-date=29 July 2016}}</ref> Between 1950 and 1953 he worked first at the then Central Laboratories for Scientific and Industrial Research, and then at [[Osmania University]], both at Hyderabad. In 1953, he went to US on a postdoctoral fellowship in the [[McArdle Laboratory|McArdle Memorial Laboratory]] of Cancer Research, [[University of Wisconsin]], Madison (US), working in the laboratory of [[Charles Heidelberger]].<ref name ="kalyane" /> During 1956–57, he worked at National Institute for Medical Research, UK, as a special [[Wellcome Trust]] [[Research Fellow]] and made a transition from chemistry to biology.<ref name ="kalyane" /> In 1958, he returned to Hyderabad and joined the same Central Laboratories for Scientific and Industrial Research which was by now taken over by [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)]] and named Regional Research Laboratory (now known as [[Indian Institute of Chemical Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web|title = CSIR-Indian Institute of Chemical Technology|url = http://www.iictindia.org/|website = www.iictindia.org|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref>) as Scientist B.

Bhargava worked in the United States, the United Kingdom, France and Germany, and travelled in over 50 countries.<ref name ="pmbmemoirs"/> He produced more than 125 scientific publications. Most of his research career was carried out in Hyderabad where he established the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]] (CCMB) in 1977. He retired from the directorship of CCMB in 1990 to join the newly created CSIR Distinguished Fellowship from which he was relieved in 1993.<ref name ="pmbmemoirs"/>

====Establishment of CCMB====
Bhargava set up the [[Centre of Cellular and Molecular Biology]] (CCMB) in Hyderabad, Telangana. CCMB is a research organization in areas of modern biology. It was set up initially as a semi-autonomous centre on 1 April 1977, with the Biochemistry Division of the then Regional Research Laboratory (presently, Indian Institute of Chemical Technology), Hyderabad forming its nucleus and Bhargava heading the new Centre.<ref name ="kalyane" /> During 1981–82, CCMB was accorded the status of a full-fledged national laboratory with its own Executive Committee and Scientific Advisory Council.<ref>{{Cite web|title = CSIR Labs |url = http://www.csir.res.in/csir-labs|website = Council of Scientific & Industrial Research |access-date = 2017-08-03}}</ref>

====Policy maker in Indian science====
Bhargava was a well-known critic of Indian governmental policies, and attained the post of vice-chairman in the [[National Knowledge Commission]].<ref>{{cite news|title=National Knowledge Commission constituted|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=9576|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=Press Information Bureau, Government of India|date=2 June 2005}}</ref> He served as a member in the [[National Security Advisory Board]] and nominee of the [[Supreme Court of India]] on the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee of the Government of India. He opposed the hasty approval of [[GM foods]] in India, and called for more testing and setting up of an independent regulatory body for generation of [[biosafety]] data of GM crops.<ref>{{cite news|title=PM reconstitutes National Security Advisory Board|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=37342|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=Press Information Bureau, Government of India|date=11 April 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Cultivation of GM food crops- Prospects and effects|url=http://164.100.47.134/lsscommittee/Agriculture/15_Agriculture_37.pdf|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=Ministry of Agriculture. Government of India|date=August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510151958/http://164.100.47.134/lsscommittee/Agriculture/15_Agriculture_37.pdf|archive-date=10 May 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also opposed the [[Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India]] (BRAI) Bill, calling it "unconstitutional, unethical, unscientific, self-contradictory, and not people-oriented".<ref>{{Cite news|title = Unconstitutional, unethical, unscientific|url = http://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/article2752711.ece?homepage=true|newspaper = The Hindu|date = 2011-12-28|access-date = 2015-10-29|issn = 0971-751X}}</ref> He was the only scientist in the CSIR who had the will to support [[Shiva Ayyadurai]], an expatriate scientist who was sacked from the CSIR by [[Samir Brahmachari]] when he authored a report that was critical of the CSIR leadership, alleging corruption, cronyism and nepotism.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Koshy|first1=Jacob|title=Ex-Padma Bhushan Pushpa Bhargava's Half A Century Of Dissent|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.in/2015/10/29/pushpa_0_n_8415688.html|access-date=20 January 2016|work=The Huffington Post|date=29 October 2015}}</ref> On 30 October 2009, he wrote a personal letter to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh requesting him to meet with Ayyadurai and review his report. He stated in his letter: "I have gone through Dr. Ayyadurai's report ''CSIR Tech: Path Forward'' and find it to be excellent." He also wrote in his letter that he believed Ayyadurai's criticisms on the functioning of CSIR were valid.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Reddy|first1=Prashant|title=CSIR Tech. Pvt. Ltd: Its controversial past and its uncertain future|url=http://spicyip.com/2012/05/csir-tech-pvt-ltd-its-controversial.html|access-date=23 January 2016|work=SpicyIP|date=20 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Letter from Dr. Pushpa M. Bhargava to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Ayyadurai's report|url=https://drive.google.com/a/vashiva.com/file/d/0Bxi2TzVXul5ZcUxpMW5pNU1MOGs/view|access-date=23 January 2016|date=30 October 2009}}</ref>

====Rationalism and science popularisation====
Bhargava has long been involved in the promotion of science and rationality and opposing superstition. He has been associated with the Association of Scientific Workers in India (ASWI) which was established in 1946 as a [[trade union]] of scientists, one of the main objectives of which was to develop [[scientific temper]].<ref>{{cite news|title=International Conference on Science Communication for Science Temper|url=http://www.niscair.res.in/Downloadables/Press_Release_sci_temper.pdf|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=National Institute of Science Communication And Information Resources}}</ref>

In 1963, Bhargava, along with [[Satish Dhawan]] and Abdur Rahman, the historian of science, felt the need to set up a national society for the promotion of scientific temper. Thus they launched the Society for the Promotion  of Scientific Temper at an international symposium on [[nucleic acids]] held in the then Regional Research Laboratory at Hyderabad in January 1964.<ref>Bhargava P.M. and Chakrabarti C. 2008. Angels, Devil and Science. NATIONAL BOOK TRUST, INDIA</ref>

Bhargava has participated in many debates related to science and superstitions and criticised the deplorable lack of [[scientific temper]] in society. He has been one of a few rationalists in India to raise voice against influential religious priests and gurus.<ref>{{Cite news|title = The phenomenon of Satya Sai Baba|url = http://www.thehindu.com/opinion/open-page/the-phenomenon-of-satya-sai-baba/article2019362.ece|newspaper = The Hindu|date = 2011-05-14|access-date = 2015-10-29|issn = 0971-751X}}</ref> His book ''The Angels, Devil and Science'' deals with the very subject of scientific temper in India.<ref name="nbtindia.gov.in">{{Cite web|title = Welcome to National Book Trust India|url = http://www.nbtindia.gov.in/books_detail__11__popular-science__152__angels-devil-and-science.nbt|website = www.nbtindia.gov.in|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref> He played an important role in having scientific temper incorporated as a fundamental duty of the citizens of India, in the [[Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India|42nd constitutional amendment]] in 1976. He was one of the key architects of the widely known '[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ycpCwjyW_C73p4lo4HlqwChVbM3O9RmU-qbxh6W8pjQ/preview Statement on Scientific temper]', issued jointly by a group of liberal, committed and rational high-achievers of the country.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bhargava|first1=PM|title=Scientists without a scientific temper|work=The Hindu|date=17 January 2015}}</ref> The statement issued in 1981, has not only been debated and discussed in several forums, but continues to be referred to in writings and speeches even today.

During the NDA rule in 2000, the Government of India decided to ask universities to introduce academic courses and offer science degrees in astrology.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ramachandran|first1=R|title=Degrees of pseudo-science|url=http://www.frontline.in/static/html/fl1807/18070990.htm|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=www.frontline.in|date=2001}}</ref> Bhargava and others, who are not named, filed a writ petition to oppose it. The write petition was dismissed by the Andhra Pradesh High Court, and the Justice Sinha did not impose any punitive costs for bringing this meritless petition to the court.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15849/|title=Dr. P.M. Bhargava And Others vs University Grants Commission, ... on 27 April, 2001|website=indiankanoon.org|access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title = Scientists oppose move to introduce astrology courses|url = http://www.thehindu.com/2001/04/20/stories/0220000x.htm|archive-url = https://archive.today/20141017151554/http://www.thehindu.com/2001/04/20/stories/0220000x.htm|url-status = dead|archive-date = 17 October 2014|date = 20 April 2001|newspaper = [[The Hindu]]|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref> Bhargava also challenged the concerned Ministry in the Supreme Court through a [[Public Interest Litigation]] which was dismissed by the [[Supreme Court of India]].<ref>{{Cite news| title=Introduction of Vedic astrology courses in varsities upheld|date=6 May 2004 | url=https://www.thehindu.com/2004/05/06/stories/2004050602931400.htm| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090625190535/http://www.thehindu.com/2004/05/06/stories/2004050602931400.htm| url-status=dead| archive-date=25 June 2009| newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=10 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://judis.nic.in/supremecourt/qrydisp.asp?tfnm=26188 |title=Archived copy |access-date=17 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050312205612/http://judis.nic.in/supremecourt/qrydisp.asp?tfnm=26188 |archive-date=12 March 2005 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Death===
Bhargava died on 1 August 2017, aged 89 at [[Hyderabad, India]].<ref>{{Cite news|title = Pushpa Bhargava, Scientist And Activist, Dies At 89  |url = http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/pushpa-bhargava-scientist-and-activist-dies-at-89/article19403218.ece |newspaper = The Hindu |date = August 2017 |access-date = 2017-08-03|last1 = Koshy |first1 = Jacob |last2 = Naninsetti |first2 = Serish }}</ref>

==Awards==
Bhargava received [[Padma Bhushan]] from the [[President of India]] in 1986,<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Awards | publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India | date=2015 | access-date=21 July 2015}}</ref> but returned it in 2015 as an act of protest against the Indian government's active erosion of spaces for dissent within the country.<ref>{{cite news|title=Worried over India's future, scientist P.M. Bhargava to return Padma Bhushan|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/p-m-bhargava-to-return-padma-bhushan-award-worried-over-indias-future/article7817665.ece|newspaper=The Hindu|date=29 October 2015|access-date=29 October 2015|last1=Mallikarjun|first1=Y.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url = http://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/scientist-p-m-bhargava-to-return-padma-bhushan-to-protest-govts-attack-on-rationalism-reasoning/|title = Scientist Bhargava to return his Padma award|date = 2 November 2015|work = [[Indianexpress.com]]}}</ref>

== Books ==
The books co-authored by Bhargava include:
* ''Proteins of Seminal Plasma'', published by John Wiley, New York (1990); co-authors S. Shivaji, Karl Heinz Scheit, {{ISBN|978-0-471-84685-7}}
* ''The Saga of Indian Science since Independence: In a Nutshell'', published by Universities Press (2003); co-author Chandana Chakrabarti, {{ISBN|81-7371-435-5}}
* ''Angels, Devil, and Science: A Collection of Articles on Scientific Temper'', published by National Book Trust (2007); co-author Chandana Chakrabarti, {{ISBN|978-81-237-5184-9}}
* ''Agenda for the Nation: An Untold Story of the UPA Government'', published by Mapin Publishing Pvt.Ltd. (2014); co-author Chandana Chakrabarti, {{ISBN|1-935677-45-4}}
* ''The Two Faces of Beauty: Science and Art'', published by Mapin Publishing Pvt.Ltd. (2014); co-author Chandana Chakrabarti, {{ISBN|1-935677-24-1}}
